## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from publisher-disclosed practices (Wiley Personnel Psychology) and domain knowledge of I/O psychology editorial culture. Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High — international I/O psychology authorship |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — workplace diversity, gender, race × employment well-represented |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Industrial / organizational psychology — selection, recruitment, performance management, leadership, training, work motivation, organizational behavior |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **substantial I/O psychology contribution** — selection / performance / leadership / motivation theory + empirical test. Strong methodological rigor expected (SIOP-aligned).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Manuscripts redirected to broader management or general-psychology venues if I/O contribution unclear.

| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |

| Mixed methods | 3 | Accepted with quantitative dominance |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed — Personnel Psych has strong meta-analysis tradition |
| Psychometric | 5 | Distinctive strength |

Reviewers from I/O psychology research community — SIOP-affiliated faculty and senior practitioners. Common demands: "Practical workplace implications?", "Multi-source / multi-method validation?", "Generalizability across organizations?".

| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International I/O psychology programs; SIOP overlap | https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/17446570 |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Manuscripts outside I/O psychology scope
- Pure qualitative submissions without I/O empirical backing
- AI use without disclosure
- Manuscripts framed primarily for non-I/O audiences (consider Journal of Management, Academy of Management Journal)

### Soft Tax

Low for I/O empirical tradition authors. Wiley editorial cycle moderate; meta-analyses are a strong fit.

### Best Suited For

- Selection / personnel testing research
- Performance management studies
- Leadership empirical work
- Work motivation and engagement
- Training and development RCTs
- I/O meta-analyses
- Workplace diversity quantitative studies

### Not Recommended For

- Pure qualitative workplace ethnography
- Critical / discursive workplace studies
- Non-I/O management focus (consider AMJ, JoM)
- Pure social psychology

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Applied Psychology](./journal-of-applied-psychology.md) | APA flagship I/O peer; comparable scope |
| 2 | [Journal of Occupational Health Psychology](./journal-of-occupational-health-psychology.md) | If workplace-health focused |
| 3 | [Journal of Applied Social Psychology](./journal-of-applied-social-psychology.md) | If applied-social angle |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from J Applied Psych as "good but not flagship-level," Personnel Psychology is the closest Wiley peer with similar empirical-multistudy paradigm.
